rv.q: What is undeniably real is Ming-Trent’s infectious energy and humor, which he firmly established as a performer.

He found himself homeless at age 16 after his drug-addicted father left home and his unloving mother subsequently threw him out of the house. He got on a Greyhound bus to New York City to pursue an acting career after discovering a love of the Bard in a class taught by his school’s football coach.
He’s a natural Falstaff — a role he’s played more than once — with his prominent belly, ebullient nature, and mellifluous voice that can seem either elevated or down-home as needed.
